akhfash:1-1.t: As for ﴿إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنشَقَّتْ﴾, it is in the sense of ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلإِنسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحاً فَمُلاَقِيهِ﴾ [6] ﴿إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنشَقَّتْ﴾, by way of putting forward and putting back (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr, inversion).

akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ﴾, that is: and it was right for it (وَحُقَّ لَها).

akhfash:23-23.t: [And He said] ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ﴾: you say "أَوْعيتُ في قلبي كذا وكذا" ("I stored such-and-such in my heart"), as you say "أَوْعَيْتُ الزادَ في الوِعاء" ("I put the provisions in the container"); and you say "وَعَتْ أُذُنِي" ("my ear retained"), and He said ﴿وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌ وَاعِيَةٌ﴾.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْشَقَّتْ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَأَذِنَتْ﴾: it listened and obeyed in being split ﴿لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ﴾, that is, and it is rightly due from it that it listen and obey.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ﴾: its extent is increased, as a hide is stretched, and no building or mountain remains upon it.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا﴾ of the dead out onto its surface ﴿وَتَخَلَّتْ﴾ from it.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَأَذِنَتْ﴾: it listened and obeyed in that ﴿لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ﴾. All of that will be on the Day of Resurrection. The apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا» and of what is conjoined to it is omitted, indicated by what follows it; its implied form is "man will meet his deeds."

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ﴾: striving in your work ﴿إِلَى﴾ the meeting with ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ — that is death — ﴿كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ﴾, that is, meeting your aforementioned deeds, good or evil, on the Day of Resurrection.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ﴾ — the record of his deeds — ﴿بِيَمِينِهِ﴾: he is the believer.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا﴾: it is the presentation of his deeds to him, as in the hadith of the two Ṣaḥīḥs, in which it says: "Whoever is cross-examined in the reckoning is ruined"; and after the presentation he is pardoned.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَيَنْقَلِبُ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ﴾ in the Garden ﴿مَسْرُورًا﴾ at that.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ﴾: he is the disbeliever; his right hand is chained to his neck and his left hand is placed behind his back, and with it he takes his record.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُو﴾, upon seeing what is in it, ﴿ثُبُورًا﴾: he calls out for his destruction, saying «يا ثبوراه» ("O my destruction!").

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَيَصْلَى سَعِيرًا﴾: he enters the intense Fire. In one reading it is with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the ṣād and a doubled lām [i.e. «ويُصَلَّى»].

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ فِي أَهْلِهِ﴾ — his kinsfolk in the world — ﴿مَسْرُورًا﴾: exultant in following his desires.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَنْ﴾: lightened (mukhaffafa) from the heavy «أنّ», its noun (ism) being omitted, that is, «أنه» ﴿لَنْ يَحُورَ﴾: will return to his Lord.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿بَلَى﴾: he will return to Him. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّهُ كَانَ بِهِ بَصِيرًا﴾: knowing of his return to Him.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿فَلَا أُقْسِمُ﴾: «لا» is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿بِالشَّفَقِ﴾: it is the redness on the horizon after sunset.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ﴾: gathered in — whatever enters into it of animals and other things.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا اتَّسَقَ﴾: came together and its light became complete; that is on the white nights.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿لَتَرْكَبُنَّ﴾, O people. Its original form is «تركبوننّ»: the nūn of the nominative was dropped because of the succession of identical letters, and the wāw because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ﴿طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ﴾: state after state, namely death, then life, and the states of the Resurrection that come after it.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿فَمَا لَهُمْ﴾, that is, the disbelievers, ﴿لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, that is, what prevents them from belief, or what argument do they have for abandoning it despite the existence of its proofs?

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَ﴾ what is wrong with them ﴿إِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقُرْآنُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ﴾: submit, by believing in it because of its inimitability?

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ the Resurrection and other things.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ﴾: they gather in their records of disbelief, denial and evil deeds.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾: but ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ﴾: not cut off, not diminished, and not held over them as a favour.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿إِذَا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿السَّماءُ﴾: fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned after it; ﴿انْشَقَّتْ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is explicative, and the implied clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَأَذِنَتْ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لِرَبِّها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿وَحُقَّتْ﴾: a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَإِذَا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the discourse is conjoined to what precedes it and its i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:4-4.t: The clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: Its i'rab has already been given.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾: يا is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾: badal (substitute); ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿كادِحٌ﴾: its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause and the vocative clause are both initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and have no grammatical position; ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كادح; ﴿كَدْحاً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿فَمُلاقِيهِ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction and ﴿ملاقيه﴾ is conjoined to كادح.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿أما﴾ is a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أُوتِيَ﴾: a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من; ﴿كِتابَهُ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿بِيَمِينِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿فَسَوْفَ﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿سوف﴾ is for the future; ﴿يُحاسَبُ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿حِساباً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿يَسِيراً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of من.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وَيَنْقَلِبُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿إِلى أَهْلِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿مَسْرُوراً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:10-11.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿أَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ﴾: its i'rab has already been given; ﴿كِتابَهُ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَراءَ﴾: accusative by removal of the preposition; ﴿ظَهْرِهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَسَوْفَ﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); ﴿سوف يَدْعُوا﴾: سوف is for the future, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of من; ﴿ثُبُوراً﴾: direct object.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَيَصْلى﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿سَعِيراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿فِي أَهْلِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿مَسْرُوراً﴾: the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿ظَنَّ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is a badal (substitute) for the preceding one. ﴿أَنْ﴾: lightened from the heavy (anna), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); ﴿لَنْ يَحُورَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan; the verbal clause is the khabar of the lightened an, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of ظن.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿بَلى﴾: a particle of answer; ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿بَصِيراً﴾: the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is the answer to an implied oath.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿فَلا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿لا﴾ is redundant (zāʾida); ﴿أُقْسِمُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِالشَّفَقِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ﴾: conjoined to الشفق; ﴿وَما﴾: a relative noun conjoined to الليل; ﴿وَسَقَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿وَالْقَمَرِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِذَا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿اتَّسَقَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿لَتَرْكَبُنَّ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the presence of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent), and the nūn that is written is for emphasis (tawkīd); ﴿طَبَقاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿عَنْ طَبَقٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of طبقا.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿فَما﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِذا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿قُرِئَ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْقُرْآنُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَسْجُدُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position, and the clause إذا… is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿بَلِ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and transition; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿يُكَذِّبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the presence of the nūn, the wāw being its agent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بِما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; ﴿يُوعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the presence of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent) — the meaning of يوعون is: they gather sins in their records — and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿فَبَشِّرْهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and an imperative verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿بِعَذابٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: the excepted, accusative (manṣūb); ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾: conjoined to آمنوا; ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ﴾: fronted khabar (predicate) and postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective), muḍāf to ممنون; the clause is resumptive.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنشَقَّتْ﴾.
It splits open with the clouds.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: [132/b] ﴿وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ﴾.
It listened [and obeyed], and it was right for it to do so. Some of the exegetes said: the response (jawāb) to ﴿إِذا السّماء انشقت﴾ is His saying: ﴿وأذنت﴾. We consider it an opinion that the exegete formed for himself, comparing it with the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُها﴾; for we have not heard a response with wāw to "إذ" when it begins [the sentence] with no speech before it, nor to "إذا" when it begins. The Arabs answer with wāw only in [the construction] حتى إذا كان and "فلما أن كان"; they did not go beyond that.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ وَهُمْ مِن كلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنْسِلُونَ، واقْتَرَبَ﴾ with wāw, and its meaning is: اقترب (drew near), and Allah knows best. We have explained it elsewhere than this place.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ﴾.
It was spread out and stretched, as the ʿUkāẓ leather is stretched. The response (jawāb) to ﴿إذا السماءُ انشقَّت﴾ and to ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ﴾ is as though left out, because the meaning is known: its meaning has recurred in the Qur'an and so become known. If you wish, its response is: يأيها الإنسان (O man), as when someone says: "When such and such happens, then, O people, you will see what you have done of good or evil" — you make يأيها الإنسان the response and imply a fāʾ in it. The response to إذا السماء has been interpreted as being what man meets of reward and punishment; as though the meaning were: you will see reward and punishment when the sky splits.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ وَرَآءَ ظَهْرِهِ﴾.
It is said that their right hands are shackled to their necks, and their left hands are behind their backs.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُواْ ثُبُوراً﴾.
الثبور is that he says: واثبوراه (O destruction!), واويلاه (O woe!). The Arabs say: فلان يدعو لهفه (So-and-so calls out his grief) when he says: والهفاه (O grief!).

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيراً﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read: "ويَصْلَى", and al-Ḥasan, al-Sulamī and some of the people of Medina read: "ويُصَلَّى". His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ﴾
bears witness to the doubled form for whoever reads "ويُصَلَّى"; and "يَصْلى" is also permissible because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَصْلَوْنَها﴾ and ﴿يَصْلاَها﴾. All are correct and broadly acceptable [133/a].

farraa:14-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن يَحُورَ بَلَىٰ﴾.
That he would not return to Us, to the Hereafter. Yes indeed, he will surely return. Then He resumed and said: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّهُ كَانَ بِهِ بَصِيراً﴾.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلشَّفَقِ﴾.
الشفق: the redness in the west from the sun. [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying:] Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī Yaḥyā narrated to me from Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḍumayra from his father from his grandfather, tracing it back [to the Prophet], who said: الشفق is the redness. Al-Farrāʾ said: One of the jurists used to say: الشفق is the whiteness, because the redness goes when it becomes dark; الشفق is only the whiteness after whose disappearance the last evening prayer is prayed. And Allah knows best what is correct in that.
I heard one of the Arabs say: "He was wearing a dyed garment as though it were الشفق", and it was red; so this is evidence for the redness.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ﴾: and what it gathers.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَٱلْقَمَرِ إِذَا ٱتَّسَقَ﴾.
Its اتساق is its becoming full: [the nights] thirteen to sixteen are those in which it is full.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقاً عَن طَبقٍ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying:] Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from Abū Isḥāq that Masrūq read: "لتركَبنَّ" [explaining:] "you will surely mount, O Muhammad, state after state". It is mentioned of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd that he read "لَتركبَنّ" and explained "لتركبَن" as: the heaven, state after state.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: And Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to me from ʿAmr from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read "لتركبَنَّ" and explained: affairs will surely turn, state after state, in hardship.
The Arabs say: وقع في بنات طبق (he fell into the daughters of ṭabaq) when he falls into a grave matter. These read: "لتركبَن", and differed over the interpretation. The people of Medina and many people read: "لتركبُن طبقاً", meaning people in general, and the interpretation is: hardship. Some said about the first: you will surely mount, you, O Muhammad, heaven after heaven. And it has been read: "لَيَرْكَبُنَّ طبَقاً عنْ طَبَقٍ". Their meanings are known: "لتركبُنّ" — as though He addressed them; and "ليركبُنّ" — He informed about them.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بمَا يُوعُونَ﴾.
الإيعاء: what they gather in their breasts of denial and sin. As for الوعي: if it were said "and Allah knows best what they hold (بما يَعُون)" [133/b], it would be correct [in language], but it does not fit with the reading.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «السماء»: fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: بُعِثتم (you will be raised).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «وأَذِنَتْ» is conjoined to the implied protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «الأرض» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (وألقت ما فيها وتخلت) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «الإنسان»: ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the preposition «إلى ربك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بكادح»; «كَدْحًا»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and his saying «فملاقيه»: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «ملاقيه»: conjoined to «كادح».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The fāʾ is a conjunction; «أما»: a particle of condition and detailing; «من» is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «أوتي» is its khabar (predicate); the clause «أما من أوتي ... » is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «ثبورًا»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause «فسوف يدعو» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «إنه كان مسرورا» is resumptive; the preposition «في أهله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مسرورا».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «إنه ظن» is resumptive; «أن» is lightened (mukhaffafa), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «لن يحور» is the khabar (predicate) of «أنْ»; and «أنْ» and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of «ظن».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: (بلى إن ربه كان به بصيرا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; the preposition «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بصيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: (فلا أقسم بالشفق) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: His saying «والقمر»: conjoined to «الليل»; «إذا»: a pure adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أقسم».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «لتركبن» is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam); the verb is an imperfect, nominative (marfūʿ) by the presence of the nūn, which was omitted because of a succession of identical letters; the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, is the fāʿil (agent); «طبقًا»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition «عن طبق» is attached to an adjective (ṣifa) of «طبقًا».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «فما لهم» is resumptive; «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); and the clause «لا يؤمنون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: (وإذا قرئ عليهم القرآن لا يسجدون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is conjoined to the circumstantial clause {لا يُؤْمِنُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: (بل الذين كفروا يكذبون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: (والله أعلم بما يوعون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the preceding resumptive clause, and the preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بأعلم».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «الذين»: accusative (manṣūb) as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); the clause «لهم أجر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الذين آمنوا».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: The discussion has already preceded about what is nominative after (إذا), such as (إذا السماء انشقت) and (وإذا الأرض مدت): that it is by an implied verb according to the Basrans, and as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to the Kufans, mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate). The governor of (إذا) is "remember" (اذكر). It is also said that the governor is (انشقت), and also said that the governor is (فملاقيه). The answer of (إذا) is (أذنت), on the assumption that the wāw is redundant (zāʾida). It is also said that the answer is omitted, and likewise the second (إذا). It is also said that its answer is (ألقت), with the wāw omitted. (إذا) needs an answer only when it is conditional; if what precedes it governs it, it does not need an answer and is not conditional.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying (فملاقيه): nominative with an implied "for you are meeting Him" (فأنت ملاقيه), a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (مسرورا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (ينقلب).

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying (ظن أن لن يحور): (أن) [with its clause] stands in place of the two objects of (ظن).

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying (فما لهم): (ما) is an interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (لهم) is the khabar (predicate). (لا يؤمنون) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm, and its governor is the meaning of the interrogative to which the lām in (لهم) is attached.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (إلا الذين آمنوا): (الذين) is accusative as an exception from the hāʾ and mīm in (فبشرهم). It is also said that it is an exception not of the same kind as the first.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the answer to the vocative ﴿كادح فملاقيه﴾, or to something implied, i.e. ﴿علمت نفس ما قدمت وأخرت﴾.
﴿السماء﴾: fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned; the fāʿil is nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause made of the omitted verb and the fāʿil is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. The apodosis (jawāb) of idhā is omitted.
﴿انشقت﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya", and the tāʾ is for the feminine. The clause ﴿انشقت﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿وأذنت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and adhinat is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya", and the tāʾ is for the feminine.
﴿لربها﴾: the lām is a preposition and rabb is genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and ﴿ها﴾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أذنت﴾.
﴿وحقت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ḥuqqat is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "hiya", and the tāʾ is for the feminine. The clause ﴿أذنت﴾ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ﴿انشقت السماء﴾, and ﴿حقت﴾ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ﴿أذنت﴾.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and idhā is an adverb of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the answer to the vocative ﴿كادح فملاقيه﴾, or to something implied, i.e. ﴿علمت نفس ما قدمت وأخرت﴾.
﴿الأرض﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it; the fāʿil [Translator's note: so in the source, meaning the nāʾib fāʿil] is nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause made of the omitted verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. The apodosis (jawāb) of idhā is omitted.
﴿مدت﴾: a past [verb] indeclinable on the fatḥa; the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya", and the tāʾ is for the feminine. The clause ﴿مدت﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وألقت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and alqat is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif, which is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya", and the tāʾ is for the feminine.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فيها﴾: fī is a preposition, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿وتخلت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and takhallat is a past verb indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif, which is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "hiya", and the tāʾ is for the feminine. The clause ﴿ألقت﴾ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause ﴿مدت﴾, and the clause ﴿تخلت﴾ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ﴿ألقت﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿وأذنت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and adhinat is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being ﴿هي﴾, and the tāʾ is for the feminine.
﴿لربها﴾: the lām is a preposition and the word ﴿رب﴾ is genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and ﴿ها﴾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أذنت﴾.
﴿وحقت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ḥuqqat is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هي﴾, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. The clause ﴿أذنت﴾ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ﴿انشقت السماء﴾, and ﴿حقت﴾ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ﴿أذنت﴾. [Translator's note: this entry repeats the analysis of 84:2 word for word, including conjunction to ﴿انشقت السماء﴾, although in this ayah the preceding clause is ﴿مدت﴾ / ﴿تخلت﴾; translated as written.]

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle.
﴿أيها﴾: the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative; hā is for drawing attention (tanbīh).
﴿الإنسان﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾.
﴿إنك﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿كادح﴾: khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿إلى﴾: a preposition.
﴿ربك﴾: the word ﴿رب﴾ is a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كادح﴾.
﴿كدحا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of ﴿كادح﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿فملاقيه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and mulāqīhi is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿كادح﴾, nominative by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause ﴿يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿إنك كادح﴾ is the answer to the vocative, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿فأما﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ammā is a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl).
﴿من﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أوتي﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾.
﴿كتابه﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿بيمينه﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and yamīn is a genitive noun by the kasra, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أُوتي﴾. The clause ﴿أُوتي﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿أما من أوتي﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿إنك كادح﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿فسوف﴾: the fāʾ is in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and sawfa is for the future.
﴿يحاسب﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿حسابا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of the verb yuḥāsab, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿يسيرا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حسابا﴾, accusative by the fatḥa. The clause ﴿يحاسب﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿من﴾, and the clause ﴿فسوف يحاسب﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, namely ﴿أما﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وينقلب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and yanqalib is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa".
﴿إلى﴾: a preposition.
﴿أهله﴾: a genitive noun by the kasra, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينقلب﴾.
﴿مسرورا﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of yanqalib, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa. The clause ﴿ينقلب﴾ is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to ﴿يحاسب﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وأما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ammā is a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl).
﴿من﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أوتي﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾.
﴿كتابه﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وراء﴾: an adverb of place, accusative by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أوتي﴾.
﴿ظهره﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. The clause ﴿أوتي كتابه﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿فسوف﴾: the fāʾ is in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and sawfa is for the future.
﴿يدعو﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa".
﴿ثبورا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿يدعو﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa. The clause ﴿يدعو ثبورًا﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of the second ﴿من﴾, and the clause ﴿فسوف يدعو﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, namely ﴿أما﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿ويصلى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and yaṣlā is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa".
﴿سعيرا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa. The clause ﴿يصلى﴾ is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause ﴿يدعو﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿إنه﴾: inna is a particle of emphasis and accusative indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿كان﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿أهله﴾: a noun in the genitive by ﴿في﴾, the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the noun (ism) of ﴿كان﴾.
﴿مسرورا﴾: khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa. The clause ﴿إنه كان﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿كان في أهله مسرورا﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar of inna.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿إنه﴾: inna is a particle of emphasis and accusative indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of ﴿إن﴾.
﴿ظن﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿أن﴾: lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
﴿لن﴾: a particle of negation, subjunctive and future, indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿يحور﴾: an imperfect verb in the subjunctive (manṣūb) by ﴿لن﴾, the sign of its subjunctive being the fatḥa. The clause ﴿إنه ظن﴾ is a second causal (taʿlīliyya) clause, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿ظن أن لن يحور﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause ﴿لن يحور﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the lightened ﴿أن﴾; and an together with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of ﴿ظن﴾.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿بلى﴾: a particle of answer, to cancel the negation in ﴿لن يحور﴾.
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿ربه﴾: the noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿كان﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿به﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بصيرا﴾.
﴿بصيرا﴾: khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa. The clause ﴿إن ربه كان به بصيرا﴾ is the answer to an implied oath, or causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿كان به بصيرًا﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar of inna.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; lā is a connective (ṣila) particle for emphasis, and it is also said to be negative.
﴿أقسم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and the fāʿil (agent) is a pronoun, its implied form being "anā".
﴿بالشفق﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and al-shafaq is a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقسم﴾.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿والليل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and al-layl is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to al-shafaq, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is maṣdar-forming, or a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of the genitive, conjoined to al-layl.
﴿وسق﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa". The interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما وسق﴾ is conjoined to al-layl and genitive. The clause ﴿وسق﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, or it is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ما﴾.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿والقمر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and al-qamar is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to al-layl, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied uqsimu.
﴿اتسق﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa". The clause ﴿اتسق﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿لتركبن﴾: the lām is the answer to the oath, and tarkabunna is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn — which is dropped because of the succession of identical letters — because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent); and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis.
﴿طبقا﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of ﴿تركبن﴾, or mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿عن﴾: a preposition.
﴿طبق﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿طبقا﴾. The clause ﴿تركبن﴾ is the answer to the oath, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿فما﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and mā is an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: so in the source; since the entry goes on to speak of "the khabar of mā", mubtadaʾ (subject) appears to be intended].
﴿لهم﴾: the lām is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive as a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ما﴾.
﴿لا﴾: a negative particle.
﴿يؤمنون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿ما لهم﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, and the clause ﴿لا يؤمنون﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of ﴿لهم﴾.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and idhā is an adverb of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿لا يسجدون﴾.
﴿قرئ﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿عليهم﴾: ʿalā is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿قرئ﴾.
﴿القرآن﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿لا﴾: a negative particle.
﴿يسجدون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent). The clause ﴿قرئ﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and the clause ﴿لا يسجدون﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿بل﴾: a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿كفروا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿يكذبون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿الذين كفروا يكذبون﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of alladhīna, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿يكذبون﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of ﴿الذين﴾.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿والله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿أعلم﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿بما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and mā is maṣdar-forming, or a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of the genitive, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa) in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعلم﴾.
﴿يوعون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent). The interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما يوعون﴾ is genitive by the bāʾ. The clause ﴿الله أعلم﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿الذين كفروا يكذبون﴾, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿يوعون﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, or it is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ما﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿فبشرهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and bashshir is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta", and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿بعذاب﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and ʿadhāb is a genitive noun by the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بشرهم﴾.
﴿أليم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عذاب﴾, genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿بشرهم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿الذين كفروا﴾, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿فبشرهم بعذاب أليم﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the implied condition, i.e. "if they persist in their denial, then give them tidings".

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), or in the position of the accusative on the basis of disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).
﴿آمنوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿وعملوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ʿamilū is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿الصالحات﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the kasra because it is a plural ending in alif and tāʾ.
﴿لهم﴾: the lām is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿أجر﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿غير﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أجر﴾, nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿ممنون﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the clause ﴿عملوا الصالحات﴾ has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause; and the clause ﴿لهم أجر...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar of alladhīna, or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: إِذَا is in the position of the accusative. We have mentioned the view of the grammarians on the answer (jawāb) of «إذا». It has also been said: the meaning is "remember when the sky is split"; on this [view] it does not need an answer, i.e. remember the news of that time.

nahhas-irab:10-11.t: فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُوا ثُبُوراً (11): [ثبورا is] a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. he says "O my destruction!" (يا ثبوراه). Sībawayh said about something parallel to this: i.e. "come, for this is your time".

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: [يَصْلى is] from صلي يصلى, and يُصلى is from صلاه يصليه, when he burns him; and likewise أصلاه.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: [مَسْرُوراً is] the khabar (predicate) of كان. It is unlikely that it be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), but it is permissible, as we say: زيد في أهله ضاحكا ("Zayd is among his family, laughing").

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: أَنْ and what follows it stand in the place of the two objects. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās about أَنْ لَنْ يَحُورَ: he said: He is saying "that he would not be resurrected". Mujāhid said: that he would not return to Us. One says حار يحور when he returned. In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: «اللهمّ إني أعوذ بك من الحور بعد الكور» ("O Allah, I seek refuge in You from decline after increase"). It was said: its meaning is "I seek refuge in You from returning to disbelief after faith"; and it was said: "I seek refuge in You from decrease after increase".

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: That is: Yes indeed, he will surely return and be resurrected; [and] his Lord was ever seeing of him — of his deeds and of what he would come to — because he used to commit sins boldly, since in his view he would not be resurrected.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: The bāʾ is the original [particle] of the oath, and the wāw is substituted for it.

nahhas-irab:17-18.t: وَاللَّيْلِ: [its wāw] is a wāw of conjunction, not a wāw of oath. وَما وَسَقَ. وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا اتَّسَقَ (18): all of it is conjoined.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
لَتَرْكَبَنَّ طَبَقاً عَنْ طَبَقٍ (19) with fatḥa on the bāʾ is soundly established from Ibn ʿAbbās, as was read [in transmission] to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Sufyān, from ʿAmr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read لَتَرْكَبَنَّ with fatḥa on the bāʾ; it is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, al-Shaʿbī, Mujāhid, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. The Medinans read لَتَرْكَبُنَّ with ḍamma on the bāʾ; it is the reading of al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr. [Translator's note: the source prints both readings with ḍamma («لَتَرْكَبُنَّ»); the fatḥa of the first is supplied according to the description.] Al-Farrāʾ said: it was also read «ليركبنّ». Abū Jaʿfar said: The first reading is an address to one person, and the verb with the nūn is made indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its lightness. Most exegetes say the address is to the Prophet ﷺ, and some of them say the address is to all people, the meaning being: يا أيّها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا, لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقاً عَنْ طَبَقٍ (19), i.e. state after state. It was also said: heaven after heaven, if it is [addressed to] the Prophet ﷺ. الكادح is the one who works; one says كدح لأهله when he earned for them. Sībawayh recited: [al-ṭawīl] 553-
وما الدّهر إلّا تارتان فمنهما ... أموت وأخرى أبتغي العيش أكدح
(Time is nothing but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek a living, toiling.)
«لتركبُنّ» with ḍamma on the bāʾ is an address to a group, the ḍamma indicating the omitted wāw. ليركبنّ is information about a group, because after it is

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: It is right for it to listen [and obey]. Abū Jaʿfar said: The real sense of this is that the meaning is: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made it binding upon it, so it submitted to His command and was split, i.e. cracked open and became gates.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: [فَما لَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ — Translator's note: this entry continues the sentence of the previous one], and before it is the mention of the one who is given his record in his right hand and the one who is given his record from behind his back. فَما لَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ (20): [لا يؤمنون] is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: The exegetes hold that the meaning is: they do not humble themselves or submit by coming round to obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: [بَلِ is] for moving from one topic to another; according to the Basrans it occurs after the affirmative and the negative.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: [يُوعُونَ is] from أوعى الشيء, when he gathered it; and وعى [means] he preserved it.

nahhas-irab:24-25.t: [إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا] الصَّالِحاتِ: الَّذِينَ is in the position of the accusative as an exception from the hāʾ and mīm. It may also be an exception not of the [kind of the] first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), as ʿIkrima related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: he said: The old man, when he grows old and weak, having done some good in the time of his strength, has written for him the like of the reward of what he used to do. He said: لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, i.e. it will not be held over them as a favour.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: الأرض is nominative by an implied verb that the second [overt one] explains.

nahhas-irab:4-5.t: وَأَلْقَتْ ما فِيها وَتَخَلَّتْ (4) is conjoined to the first, and likewise وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّها وَحُقَّتْ (5).

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: يا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسانُ: [الإنسان] is a naʿt (adjective) of أيّ; al-Akhfash says it is a ṣila (completion) because it is indispensable. إِنَّكَ كادِحٌ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَدْحاً: [كدحا] is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with the sense of emphasis. فَمُلاقِيهِ is in the position of the nominative; the original is a ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the ḍamma was dropped because of its heaviness. That is one view. It was also said: it was dropped because the yāʾ here is a letter of prolongation and softness, so it resembles the alif, and the ḍamma and kasra were dropped from it. Some Arabs drop the fatḥa from it too, treating it like the alif, so they do not give it a vowel in any case.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t: فَسَوْفَ يُحاسَبُ حِساباً يَسِيراً (8), i.e. he will be rewarded for his good deeds and his bad deeds will be overlooked.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: وَيَنْقَلِبُ إِلى أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُوراً (9): [مسرورا is] accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {إِذَا السمآء}: like His saying {إِذَا الشمس كُوِّرَتْ} [التكوير: 1] with respect to whether a verb is implied or not. There are two possibilities regarding this «إذا». One: that it is conditional (sharṭiyya). The other: that it is not conditional. On the first, there are five views on its apodosis (jawāb). The first: that it is «أَذِنَتْ», with the wāw redundant (mazīda). The second: that it is «فَمُلاقِيه», i.e. "so you are its meeter"; al-Akhfash held this. The third: that it is {ياأيها الإنسان} with the fāʾ omitted. The fourth: that it is also {ياأيها الإنسان}, but with an implied saying, i.e. "it will be said: O man". The fifth: that it is an implied (muqaddar) clause, its implied form being "you will be resurrected". It is also said that its implied form is "every man will meet his toil". It is also said that it is what is stated explicitly in Sūrat al-Takwīr and Sūrat al-Infiṭār, namely His saying {عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ} [التكوير: 14], [الانفطار: 5]; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it is good.
On the second possibility there are two views regarding it. One: that it is accusative as a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), with "remember" implied. The other: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the second «إذا», with the wāw redundant, the implied form being: "the time of the splitting of the sky is the time of the stretching out of the earth", i.e. the two events occur at one time; al-Akhfash said this as well. The operator (ʿāmil) in it, when it is an adverbial (ẓarf), according to the majority, is its apodosis, whether the one expressed or the implied one. Makkī said: "It is also said that the operator is «انْشَقَّتْ»." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Some grammarians said that the operator is «انْشَقَّتْ», but many of their leading figures refused that, because «إذا» is annexed to «انشَقَّتْ»; and whoever allows that, the annexation becomes weak for him and the sense of conditionality grows strong."
The majority read «انشَقَّتْ» with the feminine tāʾ with sukūn, and likewise what follows it. Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of ʿUbayd ibn ʿUqayl, read it with an ishmām (partial rounding) of the kasra in pausal form only, and with pure sukūn in continuous speech. Abū l-Faḍl said: "This is among the alterations that affect the rawī (rhyme letter) in verse endings. In this ishmām there is an indication that this tāʾ belongs to the marker of feminine gender in the verb for females, and is not of the kind found in nouns, so that it became a distinguishing mark between noun and verb for those who pause on nouns with the tāʾ; that is the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ, and some of the tāʾs in the codices (maṣāḥif) have been written on that basis."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Abū ʿAmr read «انشَقَّتْ», pausing on the tāʾ as if giving it some admixture of the genitive (kasra), and likewise in its sister verbs. Abū Ḥātim said: 'I heard a fluent Bedouin in the land of Qays pronouncing these tāʾs with kasra.'" Ibn Khālawayh said: "«انشَقَّت» with kasra on the tāʾ is from ʿUbayd, from Abū ʿAmr." I (al-Samīn) say: it seems he means the ishmām of the kasra, and that it is in pause and not in continuous speech, because the unrestricted (muṭlaq) form is the other, while the restricted (muqayyad) form overrides the unrestricted. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "That is because the verse-endings (fawāṣil) are treated like rhymes (qawāfī); so just as this tāʾ takes a kasra in rhymes, it takes a kasra in verse-endings. An example of its kasra in rhymes is the saying of Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
4520 - وما أنا بالدَّاعي لِعَزَّةَ بالرَّدى ... ولا شامِتٍ إنْ نَعْلُ عَزَّةَ زلَّتِ
(I am not one who prays for ʿAzza's destruction, nor one who gloats if ʿAzza's sandal slips.)
and likewise the rest of the poem. Treating verse-endings in pause like rhymes is a well-known broad path, as in His saying {الظنونا} [الآية: 10] and {الرسولا} [الآية: 66] in al-Aḥzāb; and treating continuous speech like pause is also found."

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {ويصلى}: Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the ṣād and a light lām; the others read it with ḍamma, fatḥa and a doubled (heavy) lām. The analysis of the two readings has already been given in al-Nisāʾ at His saying {وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيراً} [النساء: 10]. Abū l-Ashhab, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission from them, read «يُصْلى» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and sukūn on the ṣād, from «أَصْلى».

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {أَن لَّن}: this is the lightened «أَنْ» like the one at the beginning of al-Qiyāma; it takes the place of the two objects, or of one of them, according to the disagreement. «يَحُوْرُ» means "returns". One says «حار يَحُورُ حَوْراً». Labīd said:
4526 - وما المَرْءُ إلاَّ كالشِّهابِ وضَوْءُه ... يَحُوْرُ رَماداً بعد إذ هو ساطعٌ
(A man is but like a flame and its light: it turns to ash after having shone bright.)
It is also used in the sense of "became", so that it takes a nominative noun and an accusative predicate according to some of them, and the one who holds this takes this verse as evidence. Whoever denies this puts «رماداً» in the accusative as a ḥāl. al-Rāghib said: "al-ḥawr is wavering, whether in essence or in thought. His saying {إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن يَحُورَ} means: that he will not be resurrected. «حار الماءُ في الغَدير» means the water swirled in the pool. «حار في أمْرِه وتَحَيَّر» means he was perplexed in his affair; from it comes «المِحْوَر» for the pin on which the pulley turns, because of its turning back and forth. It is also said: «نعوذُ بالله من الحَوْرِ بعد الكَوْر», i.e. from wavering in a matter after having proceeded in it; and «مُحاورةُ الكلام» is going back and forth over speech."

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {بلى}: an answer to the negation in «لن»; and «إنَّ» is the answer to an implied oath.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {بالشفق}: al-Rāghib said: "al-shafaq is the mingling of the light of day with the darkness of night at sunset. al-ishfāq is solicitude mixed with fear, because the one who is solicitous (mushfiq) loves the one he is solicitous for and fears what may befall him. When it is made transitive with «مِنْ», the sense of fear in it is more evident; when with «على», the sense of solicitude is more evident." al-Zamakhsharī said: "al-shafaq is the redness seen in the west after the sun sets; with its disappearance the time of Maghrib ends and the time of ʿatama (nightfall) begins, according to the generality of scholars, except what is reported from Abū Ḥanīfa in one of two reports, that it is the whiteness; and Asad ibn ʿAmr reported that he retracted it. It is called shafaq because of its thinness (riqqa); from it comes «الشَّفَقَةُ على الإنسان», tenderness of heart toward him." End of quotation. al-shafaq is of two kinds: the red shafaq and the white. al-shafaq and al-shafaqa are two nouns for al-ishfāq. The poet said:
4527 - تَهْوَى حياتي وأَهْوَى مَوْتَها شَفَقا ... والموتُ أكرَمُ نَزَّالٍ على الحُرَمِ
(She wishes for my life, and I wish for her death out of solicitude; and death is the most generous guest toward the women of the household.)

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {وَمَا وَسَقَ}: it may be a relative noun (mawṣūla ismiyya), or a particle (ḥarfiyya), or indefinite (nakira). «وسَقَ» means "gathered". From it comes «الوَسَقُ» for a collection of ṣāʿs, being sixty ṣāʿs. al-Wisq with kasra is the noun, and with fatḥa the verbal noun (maṣdar); «طعامٌ مَوْسوق» means food that is gathered. One says «وَسَقَه فاتَّسق واسْتَوْسَقَ». A parallel for ifʿaʿala and istafʿala both occurring as the passive-reflexive forms (muṭāwiʿ) is «اتِّسَعَ واستَوْسَع». It is also said: «وَسَق» means he worked in it. The poet said:
4528 - فيَوْماً ترانا صالِحِيْنَ وتارةً ... تقومُ بنا كالواسِق المُتَلَبِّبِ
(One day you see us in good state, and at another time she stands with us like a girded loader.)
and «إبل مُسْتَوسِقَة» (camels that are gathered together). The rajaz poet said: /
4529 - إنَّ لنا قَلائِصاً حَقائِقا ... مُسْتَوْسِقاتٍ لو تَجِدْنَ سائَقا
(We have young she-camels, true and sound, that would gather together if they found a driver.)
His saying: {إِذَا اتسق}: i.e. "became full". al-Farrāʾ said: "It is its becoming full and complete on the nights of the full moon"; it is ifʿaʿala from al-wasq, which is joining and gathering, as already mentioned. «أَمْرُ فلانٍ مُتِّسِقٌ» means that his affair is gathered together in a way that conceals.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {وَأَذِنَتْ}: conjoined (ʿaṭf) to «انْشَقَّتْ», and it has already been mentioned that it is the apodosis if the wāw is taken as redundant. The meaning of «أَذِنَتْ» is "it listened to His command". One says "أَذِنْتُ لك", i.e. "I listened to your speech". In the hadith: "Allah does not listen to anything as He listens to a prophet who chants the Qur'an melodiously." The poet said:
4521 - صُمٌّ إذا سَمِعوا خيراً ذُكِرْتُ به ... وإن ذُكِرْتُ بسُوْءٍ عندهم أَذِنوا
(They are deaf when they hear good said of me, but if I am mentioned with evil among them, they listen.)
and another said:
4522 - إنْ يَأْذَنُوا رِيْبةً طاروا بها فَرَحاً ... وما هُمُ أَذِنُوا مِنْ صالحٍ دَفَنوا
(If they hear of some suspicion, they fly off with it in joy; and of any good they hear, they bury it.)
and al-Jaḥḥāf ibn Ḥakīm said:
4523 - أَذِنْتُ لكمْ لَمَّا سَمِعْتُ هريرَكُمْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I listened to you when I heard your growling … [the second hemistich is left blank in the source].)
The metaphor mentioned in His saying {قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ} [فصلت: 11] — or the literal sense — applies here as well.
His saying: {وَحُقَّتْ}: the agent (fāʿil) originally is Allah the Exalted, i.e. "Allah made it its due to listen and obey". One says "هو حقيقٌ بكذا وتَحَقَّق به" ("he is deserving of such-and-such"), and the meaning is: "and it was fitting for it to do so".

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {وَإِذَا الأرض مُدَّتْ}: like the first; and it has already been mentioned that it may be the khabar of the first «إذا» on the view that the wāw is redundant.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {كَادِحٌ}: al-kadḥ: al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the exertion of the self [in work] and toiling in it until it leaves a mark on it; from this comes «كَدَح جِلْدَه» when he scratched his skin. The meaning of «كادِحٌ» is: striving toward the meeting of your Lord, which is death." End of quotation. Ibn Muqbil said:
4524 - وما الدَّهْرُ إلاَّ تارتان فمِنْهما ... أموتُ وأخرى أَبْتغي العيشَ أَكْدَحُ
(Time is but two spells: in one I die, and in the other I seek my living, toiling.)
and another said:
4525 - ومَضَتْ بَشاشَةُ كلِّ عيشٍ صالحٍ ... وبَقِيْتُ أكْدَحُ للحياةِ وأَنْصَبُ
(The cheer of every good life has passed, and I remain, toiling and labouring for life.)
al-Rāghib said: "al-kadḥ may also be used in the way al-kadm (biting) with the teeth is used. al-Khalīl said: al-kadḥ is less than al-kadm."
His saying: {فَمُلاَقِيهِ}: it may be conjoined to «كادح», and the causal sense (tasbīb) in it is evident. It may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "so you are its meeter". It has already been mentioned that it may be the apodosis of the condition. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "On this, the fāʾ conjoins the whole sentence to the one before it, the implied form being: so you are its meeter." By "on this" he means: on the pronoun referring back to your toil. The Shaykh said: "What he said is not necessarily so; rather it may be a conjunction of single words." The pronoun refers either to the Lord or to the toil, i.e. "meeting the recompense of your toil".

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {مَسْرُوراً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَنْقَلِبُ». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ويُقْلَبُ», as a passive from the triliteral «قَلَبَه».

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {لَتَرْكَبُنَّ}: this is the answer to the oath. The two Kufan masters (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ibn Kathīr read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ, addressing one person; the rest read it with ḍamma, addressing a group. The morphological derivation of the like of it has already been given. In the first reading, either the address to the man mentioned earlier in His saying {ياأيها الإنسان} [الانشقاق: 6] was kept in view, or the address to someone else. It is also said that it is an address to the Messenger: "you will ride along with the disbelievers and the struggle against them." It is also said that the tāʾ is feminine and the verb is ascribed to the pronoun of the sky, i.e. "the sky will ride state after state: it will be like molten brass and like red oil, and it will be rent and split open." This is the saying of Ibn Masʿūd. In the second reading the sense of "man" was kept in view, since the genus is meant by it.
ʿUmar read «لَيَرْكَبُنَّ» with a third-person yāʾ and ḍamma on the bāʾ, as a report about the disbelievers. ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās also read with third person and fatḥa on the bāʾ, i.e. "man will surely ride". It is also said: "the moon will surely ride through states, from the last night of the month, to the first sighting, to the full moon." ʿAbd Allāh and Ibn ʿAbbās read «لَتِرْكَبنَّ» with kasra on the imperfect-prefix letter, whose verification has already been given in al-Fātiḥa. Some read it with fatḥa on the imperfect prefix and kasra on the bāʾ, ascribing the verb to the self, i.e. "you, O soul, will surely ride".
His saying: {طَبَقاً}: a direct object, or a ḥāl, as will be explained. al-Ṭabaq: al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is what matches (ṭābaqa) something else. One says «ما هذا بطَبَقٍ لذا», i.e. it does not match it. From this the lid is called al-ṭabaq. The layers of the earth (aṭbāq al-tharā) are what fit over one another; then a state that matches another is called ṭabaq. From it comes His saying {طَبَقاً عَن طَبقٍ}, i.e. state after state, each matching its fellow in severity and terror. It may also be the plural of «طبقة», which is a rank, from their saying «هم على طبقاتٍ» (they are of different ranks); from it comes «طبَقات الظهر» for the vertebrae of the back, the singular being «طبَقَة», in the sense: you will ride states after states which are ranks in severity, some higher than others, namely death and what follows it of the stations of the Resurrection." End of quotation. It is also said that the meaning is: you will ride these states, nation after nation. From this is the saying of al-ʿAbbās about him, peace be upon him:
4530 - وأنتَ لَمَّا وُلِدْتَ أَشْرَقَتِ الْ ... أرضُ وضاءَتْ بنورِك الطُّرُقُ
تُنْقَلُ مِنْ صالِبٍ إلى رَحِمٍ ... إذا مضى عالَمٌ بدا طَبَقُ
(When you were born the earth shone, and the roads were lit by your light. You are carried from a loin to a womb; when one world has passed, another stage appears.)
He means: another world appeared. On this interpretation «طبقاً» is a ḥāl and not a direct object, as though it were said: "following one another, nation after nation". As for the saying of al-Aqraʿ:
4531 - إنِّي امرُؤٌ قد حَلَبْتُ الدهرَ أَشْطُرَه ... وساقَني طبَقاً منه إلى طَبَقِ
(I am a man who has milked the udders of Time, and it drove me stage after stage.)
it admits both: i.e. it drove me from one state to another, or from one nation and people to another nation and people. On both meanings the accusative of «طَبَقاً» is by likening it to an adverbial (ẓarf), or as a ḥāl, i.e. "moving". al-Ṭabaq is also what is equal to a thing, i.e. is level with it; from it comes "the signification of congruence" (dalālat al-muṭābaqa). Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4532 - دِيْمَةٌ هَطْلاءُ فيها وَطَفٌ ... طَبَقُ الأرضِ تَحَرَّى وتَدُرّ
(A steady, pouring rain with long drizzle, covering the earth, it aims and flows.)
His saying: {عَن طَبقٍ}: there are two views on «عن». One: that it is on its usual sense; the other: that it means «بَعْدَ» (after).
There are also two views on its position. One: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «تَرْكَبُنَّ». The other: that it is an adjective (ṣifa) of «طبقا». al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the position of «عن طبَق»? I say: accusative as an adjective of «طبقا», i.e. a state passing beyond a state; or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لتركبُنَّ», i.e. 'you will ride a stage, passing (plural) beyond a stage', or 'passing' (masc. sing.) or 'passing' (fem. sing.) according to the reading."
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«عن» means «بَعْدَ». The correct view is that it is on its usual sense, and it is an adjective, i.e. a stage arising out of a stage, i.e. a state after a state. It is also said: a generation after a generation." End of quotation. He means the disagreement mentioned above about what is meant by al-ṭabaq: is it the state, the generation, or the nation, as quoted above? In that case «طَبَقاً» is not parsed as a direct object but as a ḥāl, as mentioned; but he did not mention anything for «طبقاً» other than the direct object. There is something to consider in that, because of what has been said of its impossibility in meaning, since the implied form would become "you will ride nation after nation", so that the nation would be ridden by them; although it can be sound by a very remote interpretation, namely the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "you will surely ride the course or way of stage after stage".

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}: a ḥāl; the like of it has already been mentioned.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {وَإِذَا قُرِىءَ}: a condition, and «لا يَسْجُدون» is its apodosis. This conditional sentence is also in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, conjoined (nasaqan) to what precedes it, i.e. "what is the matter with them that, when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?"

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {يُكَذِّبُونَ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the kāf and a doubled dhāl. al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with fatḥa, sukūn and a light dhāl /. These two readings were discussed at the beginning of al-Baqara.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {يُوعُونَ}: this is the reading of the majority, from «أَوْعى يُوْعي». Abū Rajāʾ read «يَعُوْن», from «وعى يَعِي».

semin-durr:25-25.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين آمَنُواْ}: it may be a connected exception (muttaṣil) and it may be a disconnected one (munqaṭiʿ). This applies if the sentence «لهم أَجْرٌ» is resumptive or a ḥāl. But if the relative noun is a mubtadaʾ and the sentence is its khabar, then it is an exception that is not of the kind of exception of single words, and it belongs to the disconnected type, i.e. "but those who believe have such-and-such". The meaning of «المَمْنون» was discussed in Ḥā-Mīm al-Sajda.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْشَقَّتْ (١)).
There are several views on the apodosis (jawāb) of «إِذَا»:
First: (أَذِنَتْ), with the wāw redundant (zāʾida).
Second: it is omitted, its implied form being: it will be said (يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ).
It is also said that the implied form is: you will be resurrected, or you will be recompensed, and the like, as the sūra indicates.
Third: «إِذَا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ) is its khabar (predicate), and the wāw is redundant; this is reported from al-Akhfash.
Fourth: it has no apodosis, and the implied form is: «اذْكُرْ إِذَا السَّمَاءُ…» (remember when the sky…).

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَى رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ (٦)).
The hāʾ in «مُلَاقِيهِ» is the pronoun of «رَبِّكَ». It is also said that it is the pronoun of «الْكَدْح» (toil), i.e. you will meet its recompense.

ukberi-tibyan:9-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَنْقَلِبُ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا (٩) وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ (١٠) فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُو ثُبُورًا (١١)).
(مَسْرُورًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (ثُبُورًا) is like the one in al-Furqān.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ (١٧)).
(وَمَا وَسَقَ): «مَا» means «الَّذِي» (that which), or it is an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows], or maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:19-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ (١٩) فَمَا لَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٢٠)).
The words of the Exalted (لَتَرْكَبُنَّ): addressed to the group.
It is also read as addressed to a single person (لَتَرْكَبَنَّ), namely the Prophet ﷺ; it is also said: the human being addressed.
(طَبَقًا) is an object. (عَنْ) means «بَعْدَ» (after). The correct view is that it keeps its proper meaning and is a naʿt (adjective), i.e. a stage arising out of a stage, i.e. state after state. It is also said: generation after generation. (لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ. . . (٢٥)).
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) is an exception; it may be connected (muttaṣil, of the same genus) or disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Inshiqāq
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْشَقَّتْ﴾: it will split open on the Day of Resurrection with the clouds. The answer (jawāb) to «إذا» is indicated by ﴿فَمُلاقِيهِ﴾ [al-Inshiqāq: 6]; the meaning is: "when the Day of Resurrection comes, man will meet his deeds."

zajjaj:2-2.t:
The meaning of ﴿وَأذِنَتْ لِرَبِّها وحُقَّتْ﴾ is: it listened. One says «أذِنْتُ لِلشَّيْءِ، آذَنُ» when I listen. The poet said:
؎صُمٌّ إذا سَمِعُوا خَيْرًا ذُكِرْتُ بِهِ ∗∗∗ وإنْ ذُكِرْتُ بِسُوءِ عِنْدَهم أذِنُوا
(Deaf when they hear good spoken of me, but if I am spoken of with evil in their presence, they listen.)
That is: they listened. The meaning of ﴿وَحُقَّتْ﴾ is: it was right for it to do so.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَإذا الأرْضُ مُدَّتْ﴾: it is removed from its form and changed.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَألْقَتْ ما فِيها وتَخَلَّتْ﴾: it casts out what is in it, of the dead and the treasures.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الإنْسانُ إنَّكَ كادِحٌ إلى رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلاقِيهِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis: you are working for your Lord a work, and you will meet it; and it has also come: striving towards your Lord a striving, and you will meet Him. «اَلْكَدْحُ» in the language is striving and persevering in work, in the sphere of this world and the sphere of the Hereafter. Tamīm ibn Muqbil said:
؎وَما الدَّهْرُ إلّا تارَتانِ فَمِنهُما ∗∗∗ أمُوتُ وأُخْرى أبْتَغِي العَيْشَ أكْدَحُ
(Time is nothing but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek a living, toiling.)
That is: and at another time I strive in seeking a living and persevere. It was said: «فَمُلاقِيهِ» means "you will meet your Lord", and it was said: "you will meet your work."

zajjaj:8-9.t: His saying: ﴿فَسَوْفَ يُحاسَبُ حِسابًا يَسِيرًا﴾ ﴿وَيَنْقَلِبُ إلى أهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا﴾: we have transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ that this is the presentation (al-ʿarḍ) before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that whoever is examined closely in the reckoning is punished. We have also transmitted that whoever is examined closely in the reckoning perishes.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُو ثُبُورًا﴾, that is: he says, "O my woe! O my perdition!" — this is what one says who has fallen into destruction — that is, the one who is given his book behind his back. The proof of that — that he is among those punished — is His saying: ﴿وَيَصْلى سَعِيرًا﴾ [al-Inshiqāq: 12]. It was also read «وَيُصَلّى سَعِيرًا», that is: his punishment will be multiplied.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ في أهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا﴾: he means in this world.
As for ﴿وَيَنْقَلِبُ إلى أهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا﴾ [al-Inshiqāq: 9], it is part of the description of the believer: he returns to his family in the Gardens which Allah has prepared for His friends.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ ظَنَّ أنْ لَنْ يَحُورَ﴾: this is the description of the unbeliever: he thought that he would not return, in that he would not be resurrected. The meaning of «يَحُورُ» in the language is to return — to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿بَلى إنَّ رَبَّهُ كانَ بِهِ بَصِيرًا﴾: before He created him, knowing that his return would be to Him, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالشَّفَقِ﴾: its meaning is "So I swear", and we have explained that. «اَلشَّفَقُ» is the redness seen on the horizon in the west after the sun sets. It was also said: «اَلشَّفَقُ» is the daytime.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿واللَّيْلِ وما وسَقَ﴾: the meaning of «وَسَقَ» is: it gathered and drew together. The poet said:
؎مُسْتَوْسِقاتٍ لَوْ يَجِدْنَ سائِقا
(Gathered together, if only they could find a driver.)

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿والقَمَرِ إذا اتَّسَقَ﴾: it gathered and became full on the thirteenth and fourteenth nights.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ﴾, that is: state after state, until one comes to Allah, Mighty and Majestic — of bringing to life, raising and resurrection. It was also read «لَتَرْكَبَنَّ طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ», that is: you will surely mount, O Muḥammad, layer after layer of the layers of heaven.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿واللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِما يُوعُونَ﴾, that is: of what they carry in their hearts. One says «أوْعَيْتُ المَتاعَ في الوِعاءِ» ("I put the goods into the container") and «وَعَيْتُ العِلْمَ» ("I retained knowledge").

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿فَبَشِّرْهم بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾: the meaning is: "in place of the good tidings given to the believers of the Garden, mercy and good pleasure, make for the unbelievers the painful punishment."

zajjaj:25-25.t:
﴿إلا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ لَهم أجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ﴾: it is not held over them as a favour. The lexicographers said: «غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ» means uninterrupted; one says «مَنَيْتُ الحَبْلَ» when I cut the rope.
«[Translator's note: the source prints «مَنَيْتُ»; the root of «مَمْنُون» is m-n-n («مَنَنْتُ»).]»
